newsitem.title: USA: Florida amnesiac united with Canadian family.
newsitem.headline: Florida amnesiac united with Canadian family.

text.p: A woman who appeared in Orlando two weeks ago without knowing who she was or how she got there was reunited on Wednesday with her Canadian family, who went to get her after they saw her on television.

Police released the woman, identified as Susan Dawn Allan of Fort Frances, Ontario, after her mother and sister showed authorities family photos that included the woman, said Orlando Police Department spokesman Sgt. Bill Mulloy.

Mulloy said Allan felt comfortable with her relatives after they arrived, but her memory had not returned. "She still doesn't have any recollection and doesn't recognise her mother or sister, can't picture her home or any of those kinds of things," he said.

Allan, who turned 27 on Tuesday, was last seen on June 10 when she began a drive to International Falls, Minnesota. Her car was found parked a day later at the Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota. Her parents knew nothing of her whereabouts until they saw her on television on Tuesday night.

Allan arrived at Columbia Park Medical Centre in Orlando on June 12, saying she could remember nothing about herself, including her identity. She showed no sign of having suffered any physical violence and was carrying a purse containing about $220 in U.S. currency.
Doctors said Allan's case was very unusual because most people who lost their memory could remember their names.

Mulloy said doctors believed the most likely cause of Allan's amnesia was some kind of emotionally traumatic incident, because there was no sign that she had banged her head, the other typical cause of memory loss.
Police had no idea how she had travelled the thousands of miles from Minnesota to central Florida.
